hints: Combine the logarithms by writing $2\ln p=\ln(p^2)$ and $\tfrac12\ln(q+1)=\ln\sqrt{q+1}$.
Move the $q$-term to the other side and exponentiate to relate $p^2(p-1)$, $e^3$, and $\sqrt{q+1}$.
Square only after isolating the square root, then rearrange for $q$.
The original logarithms require $p>1$ and $q>-1$; ensure the rearrangement is consistent with these domains.
walkthrough:
Apply the power law of logarithms $k\ln A = \ln(A^k)$ to the individual terms in the equation:
$$2\ln p = \ln(p^2)$$
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(q + 1) = \ln\left((q + 1)^{1/2}\right) = \ln\sqrt{q + 1}$$
$$3 = \ln(\mathrm{e}^3)$$

Combine the logarithmic terms using the product and quotient rules $\ln A + \ln B - \ln C = \ln\left(\dfrac{AB}{C}\right)$:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{p^2(p - 1)}{\sqrt{q + 1}}\right) = \ln(\mathrm{e}^3)$$

Remove the logarithms from both sides to form an algebraic relation:
$$\dfrac{p^2(p - 1)}{\sqrt{q + 1}} = \mathrm{e}^3$$

Multiply both sides by $\sqrt{q + 1}$ and divide by $\mathrm{e}^3$ to isolate the square root:
$$p^2(p - 1) = \mathrm{e}^3\sqrt{q + 1}$$
$$\sqrt{q + 1} = \dfrac{p^2(p - 1)}{\mathrm{e}^3}$$

Square both sides to eliminate the radical:
$$q + 1 = \left(\dfrac{p^2(p - 1)}{\mathrm{e}^3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{p^4(p - 1)^2}{\mathrm{e}^6}$$

Subtract 1 from both sides to obtain $q$ explicitly in terms of $p$:
$$q = \left[\dfrac{p^2(p - 1)}{\mathrm{e}^3}\right]^2 - 1 = \dfrac{p^4(p - 1)^2}{\mathrm{e}^6} - 1$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Applies logarithm of a power/root, e.g. $2lnp=lnp^2$, $(1/2)\ln(q+1)=\ln\sqrt{q+1}$, or $3=lne^3$. Solving this equation gives $q=[p^2(p-1)/e^3]^2-1$. The solved value is q=[p²(p−1)/e³]² − 1.
